result.summary:
Verdict PASS. No Critical, High or Medium finding; five Low findings and three notes for ORCH, none blocks. Scope: git diff base/M2PROJ-20261124-01 e656e6c, 56 files under app (no .github file changed) plus the design, decisions/0138 and docs/security-invariants.md.
Q1 cause not symptom: PASS. A counted refusal of the accept route is returned (the rate count commits), every body-only refusal is thrown (rollback); the invite is spent by one conditional update after every check and after the password hash, and a 23505 on the e-mail after the claim is thrown, so the claim rolls back; no catch swallows (the one catch in services/orgs.js re-throws everything but the 23505).
Q2 agrees with the design and decisions: PASS. Checked line by line: migration 0003 (4 tables, the invites columns and rule, the two widened checks, the users guard trigger, the insert-only idea_versions with the purge exception, forced RLS) and grants.sql (the table of 4.2.4, one to_regclass block per table, no grant in the migration); the step 9a plan hook (the entry is built from the session first, exactly the four keys action, targetKind, targetId, details are copied, any other or missing key is a TypeError before a statement, the append runs before switchToTenant, the handler gets pr.plan); the 14 route rows with the six meta keys and the order of 4.3; the eight codes and AUTH_CODES 31; the three limits and the subject keys; the closed actions and details keys; the label invite and the purpose user_delete; the consent digest on both sides through the one function consentText; the deletion order of 4.5.1; the purge only under platform settings; the audit page ordered by audit_log.id; the board with a per-stage row_number limit; the stage table with exactly 20 allowed pairs.
Q3 extra work: PASS with remarks. Every changed file is in section 3 of the design. The reported choices are judged below (F1-F5). Nothing else outside the design was found.
Q4 erosion: PASS. grep over the changed files for TODO, FIXME, .skip(, eslint-disable, ts-ignore, || true, continue-on-error, set +e and console. -> no match; no test, check command or workflow file is edited; no CR; no machine path, reference-product name or secret.
Q5 idioms: PASS. Same style as the neighbouring M2.2 code: named store functions with constant statement texts, services never run a statement, errors thrown as HttpError, times as parameters from the injected clock.
CI quoting repeat: checked. No workflow file is in the change; the only `$$` in the changed files stands in app/db/grants.sql (SQL file, the existing form of the earlier blocks, run by the migration runner, never through a shell); no shell or SQL text inside a JS script uses dollar quoting.
Own checks on a fresh clone of e656e6c (Node 22.23.4, npm ci in app): prettier --check . exit 0; eslint . --max-warnings 0 exit 0; tsc --noEmit -p jsconfig.json exit 0; node scripts/check-public.js (reads only) 'app/public is clean'. The finder logic cut from the tests (node:test import replaced by a no-op) over the whole tree: import-boundaries findings for server, api and the public js and shared files [], fileFindings [], stringSql over server and db-verify [], ciFindings [], ENV-1 [], DBC-1 callFindings [] and roleSetters []. The REQ greps: set_config('app.purge_org' only in db/project-store.js; registration_mode once (db/org-store.js); is_owner_identity only in db/auth-store.js and db/org-store.js; insert into users only in those two files; update projects set stage once; delete from idea_versions once; insert into audit_log only in db/audit-store.js. cd tools: npm run -s traces and handoffs-check run at the end (see self_check).
Own end-to-end probe (the fixture harness of M2.2 on PGlite, fast hasher, app.request in-process, no server, outside the project under <scratch>), 60 checks all as designed: the gate refusal, the invite for a new organisation, stale consent 400, no consent 400, a wrong e-mail 404 uniform, accept 200 with the cookie, a second use 404, me with name, kind and deletion_requested_at, a viewer invited into an existing organisation, create 201, a viewer create 403, edit with a reason (version 2), a foreign organisation's edit and read 404 (before the role), the viewer reads, the lists per organisation, the board counts, the card (one admin_read row per call, none for a miss), the admin's edit (actor admin, the project's organisation), the audit page (closed columns, no e-mail, no address code, no hash), verifyAudit ok after every step (18, 25, 27 rows), the audit actions with their actor kinds and organisations, the admin's own deletion request 403, a wrong password 401, a second request answering the first time with one row, the deletion list, the admin delete with a user_delete token (placeholders in the row, status deleted, projects kept while another member remains, the invite's e-mail scrubbed, login 401, the old session 401, the consent row kept), a second delete 404, deleting the platform admin 403, the purge of a sole member's organisation (0 projects, 0 versions, the purge setting empty afterwards), and an UPDATE of idea_versions refused as the owner.
Expected-red list of the developers: complete by my reading of the existing tests and section 9 and 10 of the design (not proved by running, decision 0110). Backend I1 lists TX-11 (G5), MG-1 and MG-6 (G13), RLS-2, RLS-3 and RLS-5 (G12), RT-1 (G3), SS-9 (G10), CS-1 (G9), PM-1 and PM-2 (G8), IS-1, IS-4 and IS-5 (G6, G7), RA-5 (G2), RL-4 (G11), SI-1 (G19); frontend lists PP-1, PP-2, PB-6, PP-7, the CHANGED lists of the two build tests, TX-11 for the texts. For TEST-DESIGNER: (1) the I3 divergence: SI-1's test-name rule refuses M2R-1 (a digit in the prefix), so row 15 names INV-6; keep it or extend the rule; (2) the consent keys list stands twice (public/shared/consent.js and scripts/word-lists.js), CON-5 must assert they are equal; (3) planCreate(ctx, req) is wrapped by the route, TP-1 and TP-2 read the statement sequence of a planted tenant route as designed; (4) the pg-only items stay for the pg job: the row lock of the version number (M2R-2), the invite claim race (M2R-1), the purge protocol and RLS on Postgres 17; (5) moveStage and isOption, formatDate and formatTime have no product caller: PRJ-11 and KZ-* must call them, otherwise they are dead code.

issues.text: F1 and F3 are accepted-as-is items that need a line in decisions/0138 (a new Addition) so that the divergences are recorded: the copies of keysOf (reason: the gate constant lives in services/orgs.js, an import back is a cycle) and the form rules of site.css (functional forms, look question О9, G21).

The lazy cleanup of stale invites (auth-store.js cleanup) runs at step 12 of every pipeline request, so on a tenant route it runs under tenant settings and row-level security limits it to the caller's own invites (less, never more); the design (4.4, G11, N1 of the gate) says so and RL-5 reaches it through a platform route. A new-organisation invite (org_id null) is removed only by a platform request. No defect; named for the post-deploy record.

Developer I3: the invariants table has one test name per row, row 15 names INV-6 (not M2R-1) because the SI-1 name rule refuses a digit in the prefix; SI-1 is red until the six named tests exist. Accept; TEST-DESIGNER decides whether to widen the rule.

Accepted in decisions/0138 Addition 1 (N4): deleting an org_owner of a client organisation that keeps other members leaves it without an owner (my probe showed it: the viewer stays in an organisation whose owner was deleted). A LOW defect for M3, not a requirement change; nothing to do here.

Not proved here and left to the GitHub run: the row lock of the version number and the invite claim race under real concurrency (M2R-1..M2R-3), RLS, the three triggers and the purge on Postgres 17, the pg.js transaction paths with the new routes, the e2e of the ten pages.
